records.claim: Metronidazole passes into breastmilk. The amount of metronidazole that passes into breastmilk can depend on the dose and how the medication is taken (by mouth, by IV, vaginally, or topically). With oral or IV use, the amount of metronidazole in breast milk can be similar to the dose given to infants for treatment. The amounts in breastmilk might be lower with vaginal or topical use, but this is not known. Most babies exposed to metronidazole through breast milk have not had any side effects. If your baby shows symptoms like loose stools, diaper rash, or thrush, contact their healthcare provider.
